court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Santosh Lalchand Shivnekar And Another v. The State Of Maharashtra

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Santosh Lalchand Shivnekar and another (husband, father-in-law)

facts_of_case: Informant got married with the son of applicants on 25-06-2020. She alleges that at the time of settlement of marriage, though it was stated that the boy is not serving anywhere, but promise was made that he would get a service in the near future.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the applicant to show that the FIR was not filed in accordance with the directions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.
legal_principles.held: Only because Section 313 of IPC is punishable more than seven years, the apprehension of arrest is expressed by the applicants.
cited_cases: Arnesh Kumar vs State Of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273
keywords: directions of the Hon'ble Apex Court

legal_principles.principle: The court may consider the matrimonial dispute going on between the parties when deciding the FIR.
legal_principles.held: There appears to be the matrimonial dispute going on between the informant and the son of the applicants, almost immediately after the marriage.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act and IPC implications
